mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return, as investors anticipate rate hikes and preemptively sell risk assets.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3 in the preceding month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during periods of CPIAUCSL < 0.3% (Granger causality test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressures, prompting equity market participants to expect higher corporate profits and thus a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above prior month by >0.5%
failure_condition: In 100 triggered events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) after controlling for FEDFUNDS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below 50 suggests softening supply conditions, which historically precedes a 60-day S&P 500 forward return decline as market anticipates demand compression.
failure_condition: Over 3-year rolling window, 60-day forward returns do not exhibit significant negative excess returns versus INDPRO > 50 periods (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of double-digit increases in HOUST retail sales (>10%) generate a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates sustained consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During 20 such triggered events, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (robustness: bootstrapped 95% CI includes zero).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return tends to be negative as markets price in future rate hikes and discount future earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the month preceding the horizon
failure_condition: Over 100 such events, 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median return ≥ 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month declining trend in UNRATE (below 4%) combined with rising PAYEMS suggests soft labor market, which can drive a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return via optimism about cost controls.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declines for 3 consecutive months below 4% while PAYEMS is non-decreasing
failure_condition: In 50 such triggered windows, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for GDP growth proxies (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS industrial production index below 90 coincides with a 5-day S&P 500 forward return spike as market anticipates near-term supply disruptions and adjusts for risk.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >10% in the preceding trading day
failure_condition: Over 50 such events, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (robustness: 95% CI includes zero).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 3% for 4 consecutive months), the 60-day S&P 500 forward return tends to be positive as markets price in accommodative policy sustaining equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 100 such 60-day windows, forward returns are not statistically higher than during periods of FEDFUNDS ≥ 3% (Granger causality p > 0.05).
